chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'A man consulted me regarding the Ḥajj, and he was of weak means, so I advised him not to perform Ḥajj.' He said, 'May it be that you become ill for a year.' He said, 'So I became ill for a year.'

key_terms.مَا أَخْلَقَكَ: May it be fitting for you / It is appropriate that you

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of advising someone to delay a religious obligation like Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the gravity of advising on religious obligations by predicting the narrator’s year-long illness as a consequence of his counsel to a financially weak man to delay Ḥajj. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly principle that giving advice on *fara'id* (obligations) carries spiritual accountability, serving as a cautionary tale for those who guide others in matters of worship. The incident highlights the balance between financial capacity and the duty of pilgrimage, emphasizing that premature advice can incur divine retribution.
